Definition: from the base of τιτρώσκω (to wound; akin to the base of G2352, G5147, G5149, etc.); a wound:--wound.
BiblicalUsage: The Samaritan went to the beaten man and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine. He went to the beaten man, bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast and brought him to an inn.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the verse is the gospel in a single act: the stranger who stops, binds, pours, carries and pays.
